paras: No sunlight reaches the ocean's second-deepest layer, called the abyssal zone. This illustration depicts a deep-sea submarine as it explores this mysterious ocean underworld. Scientists describe the ocean’s depths in five layers.

news.title: How Did Our Galaxy End Up in the Shape of a Spiral? And More Questions From Our Readers
paras: Add as preferred source Why is the Milky Way shaped like a spiral? Illustration by Olivier Bonhomme Why is the Milky Way shaped like a spiral? The Milky Way has spiral-shaped arms, but its inner region is more complex, with a stellar bulge in the middle and a long bar running through its center.

The cause of these spiral arms has been elusive for decades. Recent work supports a picture in which colliding galaxies, or even small gravitational tugs from orbiting bodies, can create instabilities that lead to spirals. Galaxy collisions can also compress and disturb gas and dust in ways that create strange arcs, rings and spoke-like structures.
